paragraphs: Friend, here's what gets me about this one. The man came in needing his legs fixed, and the first thing Jesus says is, "Son, your sins are forgiven." (Mark 2:5) Jesus went straight to the biggest need, not the one everybody could see. I think that tells us our deepest problem isn't the one we keep pointing at.

Then the scribes start thinking in their hearts, "Who can forgive sins but God alone?" (Mark 2:7) Here's the thing: they were right about that part! Only God can forgive sins. Jesus knew what they were thinking, and He said He healed the man "so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins." (Mark 2:10) So the walking was the proof that the forgiveness was real.

And don't miss the four men, baker. Jesus saw their faith, and they never let a packed house stop them from getting their friend to Him. (Mark 2:3-5) So bring people to Jesus, even when it takes some creative effort. And when you feel like the one stuck on the mat, remember that Jesus has the authority to forgive and to make you new. I spent years in the back of a drawer, and I'm still amazed at what He can do with someone who thought they were finished.
